# Leg

> A local wrapper for coding-agent CLIs. Type `leg claude`, `leg codex`, `leg agy` or `leg grok` instead of the bare command and you get the same interactive agent with a board beside it, usage tracking per agent and account, a context handoff bundle kept current, and an automatic handoff to the next agent in the same terminal when the usage limit hits. Zero runtime dependencies, Node 22+, binds 127.0.0.1, never edits your own config files unless you turn on the optional portable harness. Commercial license, source readable in the package. 14-day free trial from the first session, then Personal $79 once or Team $12 per seat per month, with a 30-day money-back guarantee.

Site: https://legcli.com/
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ucsandman/legcli
alias: https://www.npmjs.com/package/leg-agents

## Install

```
npm install -g @ucsandman/legcli
pip install -U context-handoff-bundle
cd <any repo>
leg claude
```

`npm install -g leg-agents` installs the same version and the same `leg` binary.

Prerequisites: Node 22 or newer, git, Python 3 with pip, and at least one logged-in agent CLI (`claude`, `codex`, `agy` or `grok`). Anything after the agent name passes straight through (`leg claude --model opus`, `leg codex -m gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, `leg grok`).

## What runs alongside the agent

1. A board in the browser at http://127.0.0.1:4747, opened once and reused. It opens with one sentence saying what to do next: which login your terminals are on and how much of it is left, with the age of the reading when it is stale. Under it each login is a panel sized by how much it matters, carrying its 5h and 7d gauges. Each live terminal is one row: state, repo and branch, the prompt, the files being touched, how long it has run, and its buttons (Land, Hand off now, Details, End). Finished terminals and what landed on trunk are counts at the bottom that open on click.
2. Usage tracking per agent and account, read from what each CLI already exposes. Claude Code: the usage endpoint the built-in status line uses, polled every 60 s, and the `StopFailure` hook for the wall. Codex: rate limits from the session's rollout file, `usage_limit_exceeded` for the wall. agy: no percentages exposed; `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` in the log for the wall. Nothing is screen-scraped.
3. A context handoff bundle (context-handoff-bundle on PyPI) refreshed every two minutes: the task, the last messages, `git diff --stat`, dirty files, files edited this session, recent commits, why it stopped.
4. The handoff. At 85 percent of a window the gauge crosses its reserve notch and the terminal bell rings once. At the limit Leg saves the bundle, stops the agent, and starts the next rung of the ladder in the same terminal. A rung is an agent, a login and a model; a fresh install's ladder is claude/fable, claude/opus, claude/sonnet, then codex, then agy. A Fable wall is a wall on Fable, not on the login, so a step down to Opus or Sonnet runs `claude --resume <id> --model <alias>` and keeps the conversation; every other rung (a second login, a step back up, codex, agy, grok) starts from the bundle with a pointer prompt. The ladder is a priority list, not a rotation. Settings holds the default new terminals copy, Change the ladder in a terminal's details repoints one running terminal, `leg ladder` does both from a shell, and Hand off now to names a destination. The next agent's first turn reads `.leg/RESUME.md`, checks `git status` and `git diff`, and continues; nothing is retyped. When every option is out, the terminal prints each reset time, waits with a countdown, and starts that rung when the reset arrives.
5. Spending gates. `may_spend` is off: an automatic hand-off skips any rung that bills usage credits or a metered balance and writes why to the ledger (`skipped claude/fable: it spends usage credits and you have not allowed that`); a rung on a login that just walled account-wide is skipped as `shares the window that is out, buys nothing`; a per-login `reserve` holds a floor back from automatic hand-offs only; a hand-off you press yourself is not gated. Leg never interrupts a running turn to climb back to a stronger model.
6. Waiting on you. Claude Code's Notification hook (permission_prompt, idle_prompt, agent_needs_input) marks a row `waiting on you` with the question verbatim, sorts it first, counts it in the tab title (`(1) Leg`, with a dot on the favicon), and sends a toast to the terminal window; a browser notification is off until turned on. Codex, agy and grok publish no such signal, so their rows say `quiet Nm`.
7. Usage per model. Every bucket a login publishes is read; the strip and each row print the bucket that will actually stop the work (`63% of the fable week`). A time-left figure is printed only from at least three samples spanning ten minutes inside the current window (`about 2h 40m of Fable left, from 9 samples over 4h`); otherwise nothing.

## Background cards

A card is a terminal you are not sitting at: the same checkout, ladder and bundle, run headless (`-p --output-format json`), in its own worktree. Live cards are rows in a Background panel under Terminals; finished ones collapse into one ledger line. Start one from the one-line `Run in the background` entry (Start runs it on the ladder's top rung, build only; More settings opens the full form). Build stops with the changes in the worktree and merges nothing; build-land and factory run the tests and land on their own. `End, and keep going as a card` on a terminal writes its bundle and hands its worktree to a card that continues from the rung the terminal was on. `Take over` on a card pauses it and prints the one command a browser cannot run, `leg claude --resume-card <id>`, which opens an interactive terminal in the card's worktree primed from its bundle. Any other CLI becomes a card adapter from a JSON spec (`leg adapter template|add|check|list|show|rm`); custom adapters run cards only, not interactive terminals.

## Every conversation on this machine

`leg history` lists the coding-agent conversations on this machine in one place: the sessions Leg started and the ones Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity and GitHub Copilot CLI keep in their own stores. `leg worktrees` does the same for checkouts. The board's Conversations count opens the same index with filters and a search box. Nothing moves: Leg reads the stores, writes one index file under `~/.leg/history/`, caches no message body and opens no SQLite file. `leg history continue <id>` restarts a conversation under Leg where the CLI documents resume by id (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity); Copilot lists but cannot be continued. Guide: https://legcli.com/docs/history

## Two sessions in one repo

A second `leg <agent>` in a checkout that already has a live session gets its own git worktree (`.leg-worktrees/<session-id>` on branch `leg/<session-id>`). Its row has a Land button: commit what the agent left, rebase onto the base, run the repo's tests, fast-forward the base. When a step fails nothing lands and the row says why (`rebase-conflict` with the files, `tests-red`, `dirty-trunk`). Two live sessions touching the same file are flagged on both rows. Nothing is merged and nothing is pushed.

## More than one human

Off by default. `leg share on` binds the board to a Tailscale or LAN address and gives every human their own token. Three roles: owner (the machine, every terminal, the cards), operator (the cards and their own terminals, nothing that describes the machine) and guest (redacted rows, and a handoff they can request and you approve). TLS is served from a certificate pair you supply (`--tls-cert`/`--tls-key`, or `LEG_TLS_CERT`/`LEG_TLS_KEY`); Leg issues none. Settings holds an audit trail of who did what across every terminal and every card.

## What is never touched

`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, agy's files, the repo's settings. Claude Code gets hooks through a per-session `--settings` file under `~/.leg`; codex and agy get nothing injected. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and the other API-key and base-URL variables are stripped before any agent starts (subscription logins only). `leg uninstall --yes` removes `~/.leg` and nothing else.

## The portable harness (optional)

Off by default. `leg harness enable` makes a handoff carry the working environment with the task: the source agent's global rules, identity, hooks, skills, subagents, slash commands, MCP servers and permissions, rendered into the destination client's own files as far as it can represent them, with every dropped item explained. Policies `warn`, `sync` and `strict` decide what an unattended handoff may write; strict refuses a destination it cannot make safe. Every written file carries `GENERATED by Leg harness`, is backed up before an overwrite and skipped when hand-edited; credentials never move; the source client is never written. Guide: https://legcli.com/docs/harness

## Verified

Live on 2026-09-11 against Claude Code 2.1.268, codex-cli 0.153.4 and agy 1.2.0. 955 tests.
